title: Harden the Tunnel listener and send the reply note at launch
body:
Harden the Tunnel listener (src/control/tunnel.rs, commit 7ec3e91) on the points an independent security review raised, and close one spec gap. The forwarded port is reachable by every user on the Remote, so treat callers as less trusted. No new routes, no pipe protocol change, no new crate.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (section: The way back)
Blocked by: Tunnel listener: token, chat and status routes, reply note
Do:
1. Slot starvation. MAX_INFLIGHT slots are shared by every Remote Session; stalled tokenless connections can hold them all and everyone else gets 503, and a token holder reading a large history reply slowly pins a thread because write_all has a per-call timeout, not a total one. Give the response write a total deadline, and make the pre-authentication read deadline short (a second or two) so unauthenticated stalls free their slot quickly.
2. Hub::serve uses std::thread::spawn, which panics when the OS refuses a thread and takes the accept loop down with it. Use thread::Builder::spawn and answer 503 on failure.
3. WindowManager::add_remote_terminal launches with no Tunnel when the manager has no Project tag, silently. Tell the user (toast or an inline note in the pane) that this Remote Session has no way back.
4. GET /status over the Tunnel returns the Project cwd, a seat-PC path the Remote has no use for. Leave cwd out of the Tunnel reply only; the pipe reply is unchanged byte for byte.
5. Spec gap: "A Dispatch brief built for --on carries the same note." Today the reply command reaches a Remote agent only with its first chat delivery, so an agent started with a prompt by `foreman open --on R -- claude "<brief>"` cannot report back until someone posts to it. Deliver the reply note once at launch when the open request carries a command (through the same once-per-connection path, Ready-gated like any injected input), and not again on the first chat delivery.
6. timeout() prints the IO_TIMEOUT constant instead of self.io_timeout; a connection that sends nothing should get 408 before close.
Done when:
- a socket test shows 16 stalled tokenless connections no longer block a valid request beyond the short pre-auth deadline
- a slow reader of a large history reply is cut off at the total write deadline (socket test)
- the Tunnel status reply has no cwd and the pipe status compat test is unchanged
- an open --on with a command gets the reply note exactly once per connection (unit test on the once-per-connection state)
- the existing tunnel, control and chat tests pass
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent control; cargo test --target-dir target/agent chat; cargo test --target-dir target/agent remote
